title: VPC IaC Upgrade Roadmap and Compatibility Checks
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: produce an operational upgrade roadmap + concrete compatibility guidance for Terraform core, provider plugins, and our internal IaC modules used by Private (VPC) deployments. Deliverables: (1) a compatibility table that maps tested Terraform versions to provider versions and module releases, (2) recommended version constraints and example constraints for module consumers, (3) preflight validator scripts (CI + local) and health-check playbook, and (4) a canary upgrade procedure with automated smoke tests and rollback guardrails. Scope excludes major refactors to modules; those will be tracked as follow-up tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility table committed to repo under /deploy/terraform/compatibility.json and referenced in module READMEs
CI job added to repo that runs terraform init/plan against a matrix of Terraform + provider versions and reports mismatches
Preflight checklist and health-check runbook published in Confluence with playbook links to dashboards
Canary upgrade procedure documented and validated in staging using two customer-like VPCs with automated smoke tests
Module constraints updated to recommended patterns in at least 3 high-usage modules and merged behind feature flag
compatibility_matrix: Terraform 1.4.x: validated with registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws v4.70 - v4.78 and registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/random v3.2. Recommended for long-term LTS when customers require stability. Constraint example: "required_version = ">= 1.4, < 1.5" and provider pin "version = "~> 4.78""

Terraform 1.5.x: validated with aws provider v5.6 - v5.12 and providers that require provider sdk v3 compatibility. We saw breaking changes in aws:v5.8 for subnet default behavior; prefer exact-pinning to tested patch: "version = "= 5.12.0""
Terraform 1.6.x (experimental): smoke-tested with aws v6.0 in internal labs; several modules need minor signature updates (resource renames) — treat as opt-in and gated behind module major bump

Internal module versions: module/network v2.3.1 is compatible with AWS provider v4.78 and Terraform 1.4.x; module/kms v1.5.0 requires aws >= 4.60; module/remote-state v0.9.x has no provider dependency and is Terraform-version agnostic (>=1.3)

Provider aliasing guidance: use explicit provider aliasing for cross-account resources. Example constraint pattern in consumers: "providers = { aws = aws.account_a }" and pin alias provider versions to the same provider block to avoid implicit upgrade surprises

Statefile lock/backwards-compat notes: when downgrading provider versions, ensure plan contains no resource recreation; we recommend running tfstate diff and registry-based provider checks in CI and disallow provider downgrades in production without approval
migration_steps: 1) Run CI matrix in branch 'compatibility/ENG-18567' that iterates Terraform {1.4.10,1.5.6,1.6.0-beta} x AWS provider {4.78.0,5.12.0,6.0.0} against a canonical minimal infra plan
2) Record failing combos and open module tickets for fixes; tag module maintainers
3) Update module READMEs with recommended constraints and add example 'provider' blocks for consumer teams
4) Create preflight GitHub Action that runs 'terraform init -upgrade=false', 'terraform validate', and a plan sanity check; wire this action into our module repos

5) Execute canary upgrade in staging: pick two VPCs (canary A,B), upgrade provider in canary A and run smoke tests; if green, roll to canary B, then to remaining non-prod environments, then to production pool with 15-minute pauses and automated rollback conditions
6) After successful production rollout, publish release note and push compatibility.json into release tag
7) If upgrade causes drift or recreation, run targeted fix PR with a migration script and document manual steps in the runbook
preflight_checks: Terraform version pinned in CI and local dev e.g., tfenv setup with pinned version
Module and provider version constraints present and not using > unconstrained ranges
State backup snapshot exists and verified restore path tested
Automated plan-diff check runs and reports zero destructive changes for non-approved upgrades
Service-level smoke tests defined and green in the last 24 hours before upgrade (auth, basic inference endpoint, KV cache warm)
canary_strategy: Staggered rollout with 3-phase canary: DEV -> STAGING_CANARY -> PROD_CANARY -> PROD
Roll criteria: all smoke tests green for 2 consecutive runs, latency P95 within 10% of baseline, error rate < 0.5%
Rollback triggers: Terraform plan shows resource recreation for stateful services, smoke test failures, or latency spike > 50%
Automated rollback: trigger CI job to revert provider constraint and re-apply plan in affected accounts; alert SRE and on-call
Mitigation for partial failures: use provider aliasing to pin old provider for unaffected accounts and drain requests via routing policy
health_checks_and_playbook: Lightweight health-check suite (HTTP probes + tokenized inference) that runs post-upgrade and produces a single overall PASS/FAIL
KV cache validation: run synthetic prefix lookups to ensure no cache invalidation regressions
Disk/FS check for on-prem: validate mount points and permission changes after provider/terraform changes
Playbook steps for failures: gather logs, capture terraform plan output, snapshot statefile, open incident with tags 'tf-upgrade'
Escalation matrix: owner (assignee), on-call infra, security if secrets/KMS impacted
linked_artifacts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/modules/pull/912 -- module/network v2.3.2 bump for aws:v5 compatibility
follow_ups: Create ENG ticket to refactor module/kms to avoid tight provider APIs (post-migration)
Add pre-commit hook that enforces provider constraint formats and runs 'terraform validate' on staged files
Schedule a brown-bag for platform and customer-eng teams to explain breaking changes and support windows
Introduce a nightly compatibility job that runs against a 'canary matrix' and raises PRs when modules drift
risks: Provider major version introduces subtle behavior changes causing state drift or resource replacement
Third-party modules in consumer repos may use unconstrained providers and break silently
Statefile corruption risk during automated rollback if snapshot/restore untested
Upgrade may reveal edge cases in on-prem networking modules that require manual intervention
